core_lesson_learned: 4 sessions, 46 paired candidates, 0 GAP_OPEN. Session 4 (path-B pivot to MODERN non-craft domains) confirmed the result is STRUCTURAL, not axis-specific. The BFS-first-mover method ('usable fresh technique x under-served domain, no prior application') is capped at NARROW by a structural dilemma: (1) a USABLE fresh technique is BY DEFINITION already demonstrated on >=1 domain, so it has a sibling foothold => every new application is capability-gap NARROW, not method-OPEN; (2) a technique with NO sibling (genuinely first-of-kind) is, in a 1-6mo window, VAPORWARE (no code) => fails R13 usability. 'usable => has-sibling' and 'no-sibling => vaporware' are mutually exclusive, so GAP_OPEN (usable AND no-sibling) is structurally near-empty. The life-axis cannot rescue it: LOW-AI regions (crafts) collide via the technique-sibling; HIGH-AI regions (modern institutions) collide via the application-already-built (often a deployed vendor => CLOSED). The NARROW/CLOSED ceiling is a property of the SEARCH METHOD itself.

R16_conclusion.question: Is the usable=>has-sibling NARROW ceiling craft-specific or universal?
R16_conclusion.answer: UNIVERSAL / STRUCTURAL TO BFS. Modern non-craft domains ALSO ceiling (0/12 OPEN) and collide HARDER (4 CLOSED vs 0-1 in craft sessions), because they have research funding + commercial vendors and ZERO none-penetration niches.
R16_conclusion.implication: No further BFS search-session (any axis) is expected to find GAP_OPEN. The method is exhausted. The negative result IS the deliverable (cf. README: useful outputs even at 0 PASS).
